bullets.text: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is now the deadliest in the country's history, with at least 2,325 deaths, and is on track to become the biggest outbreak ever.
More than 100 people have died after an artisanal goldmine collapsed in the Central African Republic due to a landslide, with recovery efforts ongoing and the death toll expected to rise.
DR Congo and M23 rebels have agreed on a roadmap for peace talks following a meeting in Switzerland aimed at resolving the ongoing conflict.
Councils in NSW face increasing pressure regarding the short-stay accommodation sector, with warnings that current regulations are insufficient to prevent investors from exploiting new developments.
A major Australian study indicates that parents caring for young children with a disability are twice as likely to report poor health, constant demands, and loneliness.
A report highlights that apartment rents now exceed half of a typical single worker's take-home pay in all Australian capital cities, raising concerns about widespread housing stress.

Economists are criticising Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's communication strategy as policymakers prepare to gather at the Jackson Hole symposium, with bond investors looking for clues on the Federal Reserve chairman's plans.
The rapid expansion of AI data centers is becoming a political issue in Ohio as residents raise concerns about higher electricity bills, tax incentives, and secrecy around local development deals.

Europe has experienced its best reporting season in years, with companies in the benchmark Stoxx Europe 600 index boosting earnings per share by 18% on average in the second quarter compared with a year earlier.
